summary:
ARES - Mars Mission Control & Interactive Surface Explorer is a high-fidelity, full-stack planetary exploration platform designed for surface navigation, scientific analysis, and astronaut mission planning.

Core Capabilities:
Interactive 3D Mars Globe: Orbit, zoom, and inspect exact coordinates and famous landmarks on a photorealistic 3D planet.
Atmospheric Weather Station: Multi-station telemetry (Jezero, Gale, Elysium) with 24-hr diurnal cycles, 7-Sol trends, and a Sol hour scrubber.
Terrain & Hazard Detection: Multispectral layers (MOLA DEM elevation, slope incline, CRISM minerals), customizable hazard angle thresholds, and crater cataloging.
Astronaut Route Planner: Trajectory optimization comparing Fastest, Safest, and Science-Max paths with solar daylight calculators and elevation cross-sections.
Science Explorer & Mission Journal: Deep-dive geological archives paired with a persistent, exportable astronaut logbook.
Ares AI Companion: An unrestricted, human-like conversational AI assistant powered by LLM integration and an expansive Mars knowledge base.
Tech Stack:

Engineered entirely with TypeScript, React Router 7, Three.js, and a Nitro/Node.js backend—requiring zero Python dependencies and launched instantly via run.bat.
details:
ARES- Mars Mission Control & Interactive Surface Explorer

1. What does it do or how does it work?

ARES is an interactive, browser-based planetary exploration and mission operations platform designed to simulate Martian surface navigation, environmental analysis, and astronaut sortie planning. It integrates six core operational modules into a unified flight director interface:

  • Interactive 3D Mars Globe: Renders a photorealistic 3D Mars using Three.js and orbital textures, allowing users to rotate, zoom, inspect exact latitude/longitude surface coordinates, and focus on iconic landmarks.
  • Atmospheric Weather Station: Displays live environmental telemetry across active landing sites (Jezero Crater/Perseverance, Gale Crater/Curiosity, Elysium Planitia/InSight). Users can inspect diurnal thermal cycles, wind vector compass roses, UV radiation, and scrub through a 24-hour Sol timeline.
  • Multispectral Terrain & Hazard Analysis: Layers MOLA DEM elevation data, slope gradients, CRISM mineralogy (clays, carbonates, olivine), and thermal inertia to detect impact craters and steep escarpments with dynamic, user-adjustable hazard slope angle thresholds.
  • Astronaut Route Planner: Optimizes traverses between surface waypoints by comparing Fastest, Safest, and Science-Max routes, factoring in elevation cross-sections and an 8.5-hour solar daylight turnaround window before nightfall.
  • Science Explorer & Mission Journal: Catalogs detailed geological and astrobiological records alongside an astronaut EVA sortie logbook with local persistence and Markdown/JSON export.
  • Ares AI Companion: An unrestricted conversational AI powered by LLM integration and an offline Mars knowledge engine that explains complex astrophysics and surface survival in friendly, human terms.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Unified Planetary Interface: Consolidates fragmented GIS elevation data, meteorological tables, and rover navigation parameters into one intuitive web console.
  • Risk Mitigation for Human Exploration: Prevents rover rollovers and astronaut stranding by quantifying slope hazards, terrain roughness, and solar power time limits before departure.
  • Accessible STEM Education: Translates raw NASA telemetry into visual, interactive models that students and educators can explore without needing specialized GIS software.
  • Frictionless Deployment: Runs instantly via a one-click startup script (run.bat) without requiring complex configuration or environment setup.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The project bridges the gap between raw planetary scientific archives and actionable human mission planning. It empowers researchers, students, and space enthusiasts to visualize what living and operating on Mars requires. By democratizing access to high-resolution topography and atmospheric data, ARES aims to inspire the next generation of Artemis and Mars-generation scientists.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: TypeScript, HTML5, CSS3, Modern JavaScript (ES Modules).
  • Frontend Framework: React Router 7, React 19, Tailwind CSS, Lucide & Tabler Icons.
  • 3D Visualization & Graphics: Three.js, WebGL shaders, HTML5 2D Canvas raster engine.
  • Backend & Server Engine: Nitro / H3 (Node.js runtime), Drizzle ORM, SQLite.
  • Artificial Intelligence: OpenRouter API (meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct), complemented by an isomorphic rule-based conversational synthesis engine.
  • NASA Data Sources & Basemaps: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS), Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA DEM), CRISM hyperspectral data, and environmental data from MEDA, REMS, and TWINS.
  • Tooling & Version Control: Git, GitHub, Vite bundler.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Gamified Yet Scientifically Rigorous: Combines actual NASA topographic datasets with mission-control interactivity—such as dynamic hazard angle sliders, turnaround time warnings, and elevation cross-section graphs.
  • Unrestricted, Human-Centric AI: Instead of a dry, keyword-restricted FAQ bot, the Ares AI Companion uses modern LLM reasoning to explain concepts through relatable everyday analogies (e.g., comparing Mars gravity to Earth, spacesuit depressurization physics, and farming potatoes in regolith).
  • Tactical Aerospace HUD Aesthetics: Built with an authentic mission-control theme featuring live Martian Local Mean Solar Time (LMST), Sol counters, pulsing telemetry beacons, and glassmorphic dashboards.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Martian Environmental Constraints: We accounted for extreme diurnal temperature drops (down to -85 °C overnight), thin atmospheric pressure (0.6% of Earth), dust optical thickness, and the critical limitation of relying on solar daylight (09:00 to 17:30 LMST) for safe EVAs.
  • Zero-Setup Accessibility: We engineered the platform entirely in full-stack TypeScript/Node.js, avoiding heavy Python/pip dependencies or C++ builds so anyone on a standard laptop can launch the system with one click.
  • Offline Resilience: Designed the application to remain functional even in offline environments or simulated communication blackouts, utilizing local fallback synthesis and cached scientific datasets.
